description.value: An event-related fMRI study comparing appetite regulation during visual food-cue exposure in obese and normal-weight women.

spans.text: We conducted an event-related fMRI study, where obese and normal-weight women were exposed to pictures depicting high-caloric food and non-food items.

value: We expected that obese women would report increased appetite and would show increased activation in previously identified regions relevant for food motivation (e.g. ventral/dorsal striatum, insula) compared to normal-weight women.

Further, we expected that obese participants would display reduced activation in cognitive control areas (e.g. DMPFC, DLPFC) during appetite attenuation as their regulatory strategies are assumed to be less efficient.

value: The DECREASE > INCREASE contrast in obese participants recruited the DLPFC, DMPFC, lateral OFC, insula, and dorsal striatum. Compared with normal-weight women, obese women showed stronger DLPFC involvement, which may indicate that they exerted strenuous cognitive effort to dampen their food craving and used more effortful control strategies.
